title: DuraLynx Dedicated Reserve & Burst Intake
summary: Initial intake to understand DuraLynx's need for reserved GPU capacity, tenancy isolation requirements for regulated models, burst strategy to hosted fallback, and pilot timeline. Discussed VPC/private deployment constraints, KMS integration, prewarm/keep-alive behavior, and an on-prem hybrid fallback option. Next: pricing sheet, architecture whitepaper, and capacity bench run.
topics: current infra & constraints (AWS GovCloud + on-prem for PHI)
reserved GPU sizing & burst to hosted fallback
prewarm / hot-pool behavior and cold-start mitigation

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-29
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Owen (Redwood SE), Tom (CTO - DuraLynx), Sarah (Platform Lead), Anika (ML Eng), Rico (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial): DuraLynx is evaluating dedicated reserved GPUs with strict tenancy isolation for PHI workloads; they want to enable burst to hosted Redwood in off-hours, but must maintain KMS control and audit logs. Interested in pilot within 3-6 weeks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're recorded — quick intros?
[00:06] Tom: Hey I'm Tom, CTO at DuraLynx, we run a mix of GovCloud and some on-prem for PHI.
[00:11] Sarah: Sarah, Platform Lead — looking after infra and sec requirements.
[00:14] Anika: Anika, ML engineer — will run the benchmark and integrate models.
[00:17] Rico: Rico, procurement — i'll help with contracts and timeline.
[00:20] Maya: Great. Owen from my side is the SE, he'll cover technical details and how our dedicated offering works. Owen, quick wave?
[00:28] Owen: Yep hi all. So to set expectations, we'll cover reserved pool sizing, tenancy options, pre-warming, and how burst routing to hosted works if needed.
[00:36] Tom: High-level goal: we need predictable cost and latency for production models that touch PHI. We're evaluating three options: full on-prem private deployment, Redwood Dedicated in GovCloud with strict isolation, or hosted with heavy encryption/controls.
[00:50] Maya: Understood. Can you share current traffic profile? qps, peak windows?
[00:55] Anika: Right now experiments peak at 120 QPS but steady day is 8–12 QPS. For prod we expect 350 QPS burst to 800 QPS for short windows — like 3–5 minutes during batch ingest.
[01:10] Owen: Okay that kind of spiky pattern maps to reserved capacity + warm pool. We normally size a dedicated reserved pool to handle baseline plus a prewarm to absorb short bursts; beyond that we can route overflow to hosted or a separate burst fleet.
[01:26] Sarah: Our constraint: any routing to hosted must not expose raw PHI to a third-party control plane. KMS must be customer-managed. Is that doable?
[01:36] Owen: We support KM S integrations — you can bring your own keys via KMS or HSM, and audit logs will be retained in your VPC, but there's a nuance: if you burst to hosted, you need to decide whether you want payload redaction or tokenization before leaving your boundary.
[01:50] Tom: Hmm, tokenization might be required. We can't send unredacted PHI outside GovCloud. Could we do host-to-host peering to a Redwood GovCloud tenancy?
[01:58] Owen: Yes, GovCloud tenancy is possible; we can set up VPC peering and private routing so traffic stays within GovCloud regions. That keeps the control plane integrations local. Alternatively a hybrid where pre-sanitization happens on-prem before sending to hosted.
[02:13] Maya: Quick question for procurement timeline, Rico? any constraints?
[02:16] Rico: We'd like to have a PO executed within 6–8 weeks, but pilot contract needs to be short — 30 day eval or so.
[02:23] Maya: We can do a pilot contract, yep.
[02:25] Anika: On the model side, we're running Llama-based 30B and one proprietary LLM we can't open-source. Concerned about quantization and perf. How does Redwood handle custom models?
[02:36] Owen: We can host customer models in Dedicated; we do model onboarding that tests quantization profiles and kernel selection. For some proprietary models on-prem is preferred to avoid external model file transfers.
[02:47] Tom: Performance target is p99 under 400ms for inference on short prompts. Can Redwood meet that on reserved infra?
[02:54] Owen: For 30B-class models on A100/H100 equivalents, with proper batching and KV cache, p99 in sub-400ms is feasible at modest sequence lengths. We can prototype with your prompt sets to validate.
[03:07] Sarah: What about prewarm cost? We worry about paying to keep GPUs hot.
[03:12] Owen: There's a tradeoff: warm pool policy allows short prewarmed instances for X hours to absorb burst without full reservation. Reserved capacity pricing is lower per unit; hot-pool can be configured to minimize hours. We'll share a pricing matrix.
[03:24] Tom: Are there tenancy options for stronger isolation — like single-tenant nodes per customer or even per-team?
[03:29] Owen: Yes, Dedicated supports single-tenant pools and node-level fencing. You can reserve entire nodes for strict isolation. That increases cost, of course, but satisfies strict tenant separation and auditability.
[03:40] Anika: How do you handle KV cache warms across tenants? if we have single-tenant nodes do we still get caching benefits?
[03:46] Owen: Yes, KV cache is per model instance, per node; single-tenant helps because you don't evict others' caches. Also useful for long chat contexts to keep state.
[03:55] Sarah: Encryption at rest in our control is mandatory. You said KMS — do we supply keys that are never exported?
[04:01] Owen: Correct. We integrate with customer-managed KMS; keys never leave your HSM. We can also produce audit logs showing key usage.
[04:09] Tom: A practical question: if we have on-prem air-gapped for training and inference, can Redwood ship a private bundle to our data center?
[04:18] Owen: We have an on-prem package for regulated customers. It includes a private control plane that can run behind your firewall. For fully air-gapped, we coordinate a binary bundle, but model onboarding may be manual. That tends to be a longer lead time.
[04:31] Sarah: Lead time — what are we looking at for a pilot in GovCloud vs on-prem?
[04:35] Maya: GovCloud Dedicated pilot typically 2–4 weeks to stand up nodes and get a sandbox; on-prem air-gapped is 6–10 weeks depending on approvals.
[04:43] Rico: Budget question — if we do 3 months reserved at a lower rate, can we get credit for unused hours?
[04:49] Maya: We can do burst credits in some reserved contracts — it's negotiable. We'll put sample terms in the pricing sheet.
[04:56] Tom: For burst, you mentioned routing rules. Can we prioritize critical traffic and drop non-essential?
[05:02] Owen: Absolutely, policy routing can be traffic-class aware. You can set priorities, and automatic fallback rules — e.g., try local reserved pool, then warm pool, then hosted with redaction, etc.
[05:14] Anika: Any guidance on batching — we need latency but also token cost.
[05:18] Owen: We provide batching knobs and suggest sequence-length aware batching. Also prefix caching reduces repeated token cost; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batch config tuned to your workload.
[05:29] Sarah: Security review — do you have SOC2 and penetration test reports?
[05:33] Maya: Yes, we'll share SOC2 and our pen test summary. For Dedicated/Private, we also supply architecture diagrams and KMS integration docs.
[05:41] Tom: Who else do we need to involve from your side for the bench run?
[05:44] Maya: Owen will drive the bench. Also Solutions Engineering for any model-specific tweaks.
[05:49] Owen: For the bench run ideally we get your prompt sets, sample tokens per request, and expected QPS distribution. We'll run end-to-end latency and cost metrics.
[05:58] Tom: We'll send those. Also want to confirm SLA — p99 latency target and uptime for Dedicated.
[06:04] Maya: Our enterprise Dedicated contracts have SLA tiers. We'll include sample SLOs in the packet.
[06:09] Rico: Procurement will need an NDA and statement of work template to start legal loop.
[06:13] Maya: We'll attach NDA and a short pilot SOW.
[06:16] Anika: Quick nitpick: how do you handle model updates and rollouts on Dedicated without affecting latency?
[06:22] Owen: We support canary rollouts and pinned model versions per route. You can test on a fraction of traffic before full promotion; automatic fallback to previous model if regressions detected.
[06:32] Tom: Any known limitations with embedded models for our proprietary LLM?
[06:36] Owen: Some older CUDA kernels need retuning; we do a compatibility pass during onboarding and may recommend a quantization path or different instance type.
[06:45] Sarah: Ok, timeline recap? Pilot in GovCloud likely prioritized, bench week Apr 11, deliver pricing and docs by next week.
[06:55] Maya: Yep. I'll send pricing and SOC2 pack. Owen will send architecture sketch.
[06:59] Rico: We'll review documents and revert on PO timeline.
[07:02] Tom: Great. Anything else?
[07:04] Anika: Can we get a checklist of what to provide for the bench run?
[07:07] Owen: Yes — prompt sets, QPS profiles, sample model weights access approach (if needed), and test account keys. I'll add that to the sheet.
[07:14] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the bench.
[07:18] (call ends)

Notes on transcription artifacts: occasional words misrecognized ("K-V cash" for KV cache), acronyms sometimes split ("S O C Two"), and minor speaker label shifts in the auto transcript.
